criteria.criterion: A new scorer test shows the same job records score with a bound-only cost provisional under the current rules string and not provisional under the previous v1 rules string; run `cargo test -p athena-score`.
criteria.evidence: I ran tests::the_same_records_score_a_bound_only_cost_provisional_under_v2_and_not_under_v1 and it passed. It scores one Resolution with a bound cost under RULES (v2) and gets provisional=true, then under RULES_V1 and gets provisional=false. It also checks that an unknown string returns None. Athena's full `cargo test` run covered the rest of the crate.

criteria.criterion: A gate test shows a score file stamped with the v1 rules string, whose cost was a bound, still passes the score-follows-records check, and a v2 score with the wrong provisional flag is still rejected; run `cargo test -p athena-gate`.
criteria.evidence: All 7 jobs::tests passed. a_v1_score_of_a_bound_only_cost_still_follows_its_records commits a v1 score of a bound-only cost, and both check_head and scores_that_do_not_follow return empty. a_v2_score_with_the_wrong_provisional_flag_is_refused sets provisional=false under v2, and the gate reports 'does not follow'.

criteria.criterion: `cargo run -p athena -- check --history` (or the repository's equivalent) over the repository reports no violation for the 8 existing score files, including records/jobs/2026-10/20261013-141005-hrdp/score.json, and no file under records/ is modified in the diff.
criteria.evidence: Only the snapshot was checked. `git diff HEAD~1 --stat -- records` is empty, so no record is modified. There is no `athena` package; the CLI is `athena-cli`. Running its history check here read 0 record files, because records/ is absent from the snapshot. Its 2 violations are about the snapshot's own unlanded commits, so this run says nothing about the 8 real score files. From reading the code: the history check calls jobs::check, which now recomputes each score with expected_score_under(&score.rules, ...). Under v1 the only change is cost_provisional=false, the behavior from before #129, so v1 scores without a provisional field (it defaults to false) should recompute equal. On the real repository, every_recorded_score_follows_from_its_records_under_its_own_rules runs that recompute over the committed records/. It has to pass in CI there to confirm this criterion.

criteria.criterion: New scores are written under a bumped rules string (v2); the gate recomputes each score under the rules string it carries and still refuses an unknown rules string.
criteria.evidence: From the diff: in athena-score/src/lib.rs, RULES now ends with 'v2', RULES_V1 is kept, and KNOWN_RULES=[RULES_V1, RULES]. score_job and score_records use RULES. In jobs.rs check(), the old `score.rules != RULES` test is replaced by expected_score_under(&score.rules, ...). A None result still produces the 'cannot recompute' violation. The test a_rules_string_this_athena_does_not_know_is_refused covers the refusal.

criteria.criterion: A mechanism, not prose, makes a change to scoring behavior get checked against the full history before landing: a test or the xtask ci step recomputes every historical score with the working-tree scorer and fails if the rules string was not bumped; run `cargo run -p xtask -- ci` or `cargo test` to see it pass, and a test shows it fails when a rule changes under an unchanged version.
criteria.evidence: The new unit test every_recorded_score_follows_from_its_records_under_its_own_rules runs scores_that_do_not_follow on the repository's HEAD tree, so `cargo test` and xtask ci run it. In the snapshot it passed with nothing to check, because no records/ are committed. a_rule_changed_without_a_new_rules_version_is_caught_by_the_history_check shows the function reports a v2-stamped score made by the earlier behavior. Limits are listed under findings.

findings.summary: The history guard cannot yet catch a change to v2 behavior, and it passes silently when there is no git repository or no HEAD
findings.evidence: The guard recomputes only scores already committed, and none carries v2 yet. Until one does, a change to v2 scoring that keeps the version string passes it. D108's Tradeoff states this. If Git::discover fails or HEAD is missing, the test returns early and passes; in this snapshot it passed with nothing to check.

findings.summary: Criterion 3 could not be exercised in the snapshot
findings.evidence: `cargo run -q -p athena-cli -- check --history` read 0 record files here, and its 2 violations concern the snapshot's own commits. Whether the 8 real score files, including the hrdp one, pass rests on code reading, plus the history test and the history job in CI on the real repository.

summary: The change versions the scoring rules. New scores are stamped `v2`, which marks a bound-only cost provisional, and `v1` scores are recomputed with the old behavior. The gate now recomputes each score under the rules string it carries and still refuses an unknown string. No file under records/ is touched. A new test runs during `cargo test`: it recomputes every committed score with the working-tree scorer, so a scoring change that keeps its version fails before it lands. D108 records the decision and its alternatives, and the changelog is updated. I ran the new scorer and gate tests, and they pass. Athena's fmt, clippy and full test runs also passed. The history check over the real 8 score files could not be run here because the snapshot has no records/. That outcome rests on code reading: the v1 path only resets the provisional flag. CI on the real repository needs to confirm it. Three minor findings: (1) one file outside the deliverables list, a test helper; (2) the guard cannot catch changes to v2 behavior until a v2 score is in history, and it passes silently without a repository (D108 records the first limit); (3) the history check above could not be run here.
